    StartersTattoo parlour pork spring rollsCrisp rolls of pork mince, cabbage and carrot in oyster sauceHow to make it300g pork mince1/4 savoy cabbage1 carrot2 garlic cloves2 tbsp oyster sauce1 tbsp soy sauce16 spring rolls of wrappers150ml sweet chilli sauce1 lime1 bunch coriander1 L vegetable oilFry the pork mince until browned, add the finely shredded cabbage, the grated carrot, the crushed garlic cloves, the oyster sauce and the soy, and cook 3 minutes.Cool completely.Roll the filling in each of the spring roll wrappers, sealing the edge with a little water.Deep fry in the vegetable oil at 180°C for 3 to 4 minutes until golden, then drain on paper towel.Stir the juice of the lime into the sweet chilli sauce and serve with coriander.Zoltan's popping candy caramel cornBaked caramel popcorn with white chocolate and popping candyHow to make it100g popcorn kernels100g butter150g brown sugar60ml golden syrup1/2 tsp bicarbonate of soda100g white chocolate1 bottle blue food colouring2 packets of popping candy2 tbsp vegetable oilPop the popcorn kernels in the oil and tip into a big bowl, picking out any unpopped kernels.Boil the butter, the brown sugar and the golden syrup for 4 minutes, take off the heat and stir in the bicarbonate of soda and a pinch of salt.Pour over the popcorn, toss and spread on a lined tray.Bake at 120°C for 20 minutes, stirring once.Melt the white chocolate with the blue colouring, drizzle over and scatter with the popping candy.MainsDrive-through lemon chicken and fried riceCrispy chicken in lemon sauce, egg fried rice and garlic broccoliHow to make it700g chicken thigh fillets3 eggs120g cornflour3 lemons80g caster sugar300g jasmine rice100g frozen peas2 tbsp soy sauce1 bunch spring onions1 head broccoli2 garlic cloves500ml vegetable oil150ml waterCook the jasmine rice the day before and chill.Cut the chicken thigh into strips, dip in the beaten egg, then toss in the cornflour.Shallow fry in the vegetable oil at 180°C for 5 minutes until crisp.Simmer the juice of the lemons, the caster sugar, the water and the cornflour until glossy, and pour over.Fry the cold rice in a hot wok with the scrambled eggs, the peas, the soy and the spring onions.Stir-fry the head broccoli with the garlic cloves for 3 minutes.'And then?' beef and black bean noodlesThe drive-through order that never ends: and then, and then, and thenHow to make it500g beef rump, thinly sliced1 tbsp cornflour2 tbsp soy sauce3 tbsp black bean sauce1 green capsicum, sliced1 onion, sliced2 garlic cloves, crushed500g fresh hokkien noodles2 tbsp vegetable oil2 spring onions, slicedToss the beef with the cornflour and 1 tbsp soy.Stir-fry the beef in half the oil in a very hot wok until browned, then lift out.Stir-fry the onion, capsicum and garlic in the rest of the oil, add the noodles, black bean sauce and the rest of the soy.Toss the beef back through and top with spring onion.SweetsFridge full of chocolate pudding potsStovetop chocolate pudding chilled in potsHow to make it80g caster sugar30g cocoa powder30g cornflour600ml full cream milk100g dark chocolate1 tsp vanilla extract4 tbsp salted caramel sauce200ml thickened cream4 chocolate biscuitsWhisk the caster sugar, the cocoa, the cornflour and a pinch of salt in a saucepan, then slowly whisk in the milk.Stir over medium heat until it boils and thickens, about 6 minutes.Take off the heat and stir in the chopped dark chocolate and the vanilla.Pour into jars, press cling film on top and chill 2 hours.Top each with a spoon of caramel sauce, whipped cream from the thickened cream and the crushed chocolate biscuits.DrinksDrive-through lychee lime slushieFrozen lychee, lime and lemonade blended into a slushHow to make ita 565g tin lychees4 limes1 bag ice600ml
